record.title: Mitra–Pyatov conjecture for the number of HSFPL diagrams
record.statement:
Let an FPL diagram of size $L$ have size $(L-1)\times L/2$ when $L$ is even and size $L\times (L-1)/2$ when $L$ is odd. Let $d$ be its depth, and let $S(L,d)$ denote the total number of HSFPL diagrams of size $L$ and depth $d$. Here $(a)_k$ denotes the rising factorial and $\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function. **Mitra–Pyatov conjecture.** The total number is

$$
S(L,d)=\prod_{k=0}^{d}\frac{\Gamma(L-k+1)}{2^k(1/2)_k\Gamma(L-2k+1)}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{2L+2k+3}{6}\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{L-2k+3}{3}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{2L-k+3}{6}\right)\Gamma\left(\frac{2L-k+6}{6}\right)}.
$$

Assuming the RS conjecture, this formula was subsequently proved, so the conjecture is resolved.
record.source_name: Jan de Gier, “Fully packed loop models on finite geometries”, arXiv:0901.3963 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3963

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2009); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Pyatov's conjecture for the HSFPL nest generating function
record.statement:
For half-turn symmetric FPL diagrams with $L=2n$ external terminals, let $P(L,m)$ count diagrams with $m+1$ nests and define

$$
\mathcal{P}(L;z)=\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}P(L,m)z^m.
$$

Let $Z_{\rm HTSFPL}(2n)$ be the total number of half-turn symmetric FPL diagrams of size $2n$. **Pyatov's conjecture.** The nest generating function is

$$
\mathcal{P}(2n;z)=Z_{\rm HTSFPL}(2n)\frac{3n}{4n^2-1}\,{}_3F_2\left(\begin{array}{c}\frac{3}{2},1-n,1+n\\2-2n,2+2n\end{array};4z\right).
$$

The paper attributes this conjecture to de Gier; it is stated only for $L=2n$ and $d^*=0$, and the supplied text gives no resolution, so it remains open.

record.title: Efficient oracle recognition of binary internally 4-connected matroids
record.statement:
An **internally $4$-connected matroid** is a matroid satisfying the internal $4$-connectivity condition used in the source. An oracle algorithm accesses a matroid through an oracle for its relevant operations or queries.

**Binary-recognition conjecture.** There is an efficient oracle algorithm for deciding whether an internally $4$-connected matroid is binary.

The conjecture is motivated by the absence of an efficient oracle algorithm for recognizing binary matroids in general, attributed in the source to degeneracies caused by low connectivity. The source calls it ambitious and gives no resolution.

record.title: Bannister–Ostergård subdivision conjecture for stack number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $H$ be a $(\leq 1)$-subdivision of $G$, obtained by subdividing each edge of $G$ at most once. Let $\operatorname{sn}(G)$ denote the stack number of $G$. **Bannister–Ostergård subdivision conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that

$$
\operatorname{sn}(G)\leq f(\operatorname{sn}(H)).
$$

This conjecture asks whether stack number is bounded on graphs whose edges are subdivided at most once, in terms of the stack number of the original graph. The source states that the corresponding result is open and attributes the conjecture to Bannister and Ostergård.

record.title: The 2-adic shift conjecture for involution numbers
record.statement:
Let $t_{4k+1}^e$ denote the even involution count associated with size $4k+1$, let $\operatorname{ord}_2$ be the 2-adic valuation, and let $\chi_o(k)$ be the indicator of odd integers. A **2-adic integer** is an element of $\mathbb{Z}_2$; write

$$
\rho=\sum_{i\geq 0}\rho_i2^i,
$$

where $0\leq\rho_i\leq1$.

**2-adic shift conjecture.** There is a 2-adic integer $\rho$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{ord}_2(t_{4k+1}^e)=k+\chi_o(k)\bigl(\operatorname{ord}_2(k+\rho)+1\bigr).
$$

This conjecture gives the missing 2-adic valuation formula for the even involution counts $t_{4k+1}^e$; the paper presents it as an extrapolation from Maple experiments, and no proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Dongsu Kim and Jang Soo Kim, “A combinatorial approach to the power of 2 in the number of involutions”, arXiv:0902.4311 (2010).

record.title: Extremal metric decomposition conjecture for projective bundles over curves
record.statement:
Let $(M,J)=P(E)$ be a projective bundle over a compact curve of genus at least $2$, where $E$ is a holomorphic vector bundle. A bundle **decomposes as a direct sum of stable subbundles** when $E=\bigoplus_i E_i$ with each $E_i$ stable.

**Extremal metric decomposition conjecture.** The projective bundle $(M,J)=P(E)$ admits an extremal Kähler metric in some Kähler class if and only if $E$ decomposes as a direct sum of stable subbundles.

This would give a general existence criterion for extremal Kähler metrics on projective bundles over curves. The paper presents it as a statement suggested by the compatibility conjecture; its resolution is not supplied in the given text.

record.title: The least-word conjecture for the Rudin–Shapiro orbit closure
record.statement: Let ${\bf w}$ be the Rudin–Shapiro word and let ${\mathpzc O}_w$ be its orbit closure, the set of right infinite words all of whose finite prefixes are factors of ${\bf w}$. Order binary words lexicographically with $0<1$. **Least-word conjecture.** The word $0{\bf w}$ is the least word in ${\mathpzc O}_w$. This conjecture concerns the lexicographically least element of the orbit closure of the Rudin–Shapiro word; the supplied source gives no information about whether it has been resolved.

record.title: Eli's descent-set conjecture for zero-marked cyclic permutations
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal T}^0_n$ be the set of $n$-cycles in one-line notation with one entry replaced by $0$, and let $D(a)=\{i:1\le i\le n-1,\ a_i>a_{i+1}\}$ denote the descent set of a sequence $a$. For $I\subseteq[n-1]$, write $\{\tau\in {\mathcal T}^0_n:D(\tau)=I\}$ for the zero-marked cyclic permutations with descent set $I$.

**Eli's descent-set conjecture.** For any $n$ and any $I\subseteq[n-1]$, 

$$
\left|\{\tau\in {\mathcal T}^0_n\,:\,D(\tau)=I\}\right|=\left|\{\sigma\in\mathcal S_n\,:\,D(\sigma)=I\}\right|.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the descent-set distribution on zero-marked cyclic permutations agrees with that on all permutations. The supplied text attributes it to Eli; its resolution is not stated in the provided context, so its status is recorded as open.

record.title: Extended doubly-refined enumeration formula for alternating sign matrices
record.statement:
For each $n\ge 1$, let $\left(\hat{A}_{n,i,j}\right)_{i,j=1}^n$ be the **extended doubly-refined enumeration numbers** defined in the cited work. Define

$$
X_n(s,t)=\frac{1}{A_{n-1}}\Bigl(A_{n-1,t}(A_{n,s+1}-A_{n,s})-A_{n-1,s}(A_{n,t+1}-A_{n,t})\Bigr).
$$

**Extended enumeration conjecture.** The explicit formula for the doubly-refined enumeration numbers also holds for the extended numbers:

$$
\hat{A}_{n,i,j}=\sum_{p=0}^{n-j}\sum_{q=0}^p(-1)^q\binom{p}{q}X_n(i+q,j+p),\qquad (1\le i,j\le n).
$$

This is an empirical extension of the proved formula for the ordinary doubly-refined enumeration numbers, and it does not follow from the methods used in the paper.

record.title: Normality conjecture for cut polytopes of 4-connected plane triangulations
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 4-connected plane triangulation, and let ${\rm Cut}^\square(G)$ denote its cut polytope. Normality means that the affine semigroup generated by the homogenized cut vectors is saturated.

**The 4-connected plane triangulation conjecture.** The cut polytope ${\rm Cut}^\square(G)$ is normal if $G$ is a 4-connected plane triangulation.

This is presented as a sufficient reduction for proving the Sturmfels–Sullivant conjecture, because the relevant class of graphs can be decomposed using graph sums and the remaining difficult cases are 4-connected plane triangulations. The source does not report a resolution.

record.title: The realizability conjecture for cutsets in polytopes
record.statement: Let $P$ be a $d$-polytope with graph $G_P$, and let a cutset be a set of vertices selected for removal by a hyperplane. Properties 1 and 2 of Proposition are connectedness of the cutset and connectedness of its complement in $G_P$. **Realizability conjecture.** For $d\geq 3$, every cutset satisfying properties 1 and 2 of Proposition is realizable. The claim extends the preceding proved three-dimensional result to all dimensions $d\geq 3$; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Pomerance conjecture on four-term minimal zero-sum sequences
record.statement:
Let $Z_n$ be the cyclic group of $n$ elements. A sequence is **minimal zero-sum** if its sum is zero in $Z_n$ and no proper nonempty subsequence has sum zero. Its index is

$$
\operatorname{Index}(S)=\min_{(m,n)=1}\{\sigma(|mS|_n)\}.
$$

**Pomerance conjecture.** If $n$ is a positive integer with $(n,6)=1$ and $S$ is a minimal zero-sum sequence in $Z_n$ with $|S|=4$, then

$$
\operatorname{Index}(S)=n.
$$

Results cited in the paper establish the analogous assertion for minimal zero-sum sequences of length at most three and of length at least $n/2+1$, while the four-term case under the stated coprimality condition is presented as conjectural.
record.source_name: Weidong Gao, Yuanlin Li, Jiangtao Peng, Chris Plyley and Guoqing Wang, “On the Index of Sequences over Cyclic Groups”, arXiv:0909.2461 (2011).

record.title: Factorization conjecture for the characteristic polynomial of the asymmetric annihilation Markov matrix
record.statement:
Let $M_L$ be the Markov matrix for a system of size $L$, with characteristic polynomial $P_L(x)$. Define

$$
A_L(x)=\prod_{k=0}^{\lceil L/2\rceil}(x+2k)^{\binom{L-1}{2k}},\qquad B_L(x)=\prod_{k=0}^{\lfloor L/2\rfloor}(x+2k+1)^{\binom{L-1}{2k+1}}.
$$

**Characteristic-polynomial factorization conjecture.** The characteristic polynomial and its successive ratios are

$$
P_L(x)=A_L(x)A_L(x+2\alpha+\beta)B_L(x+\beta)B_L(x+2\alpha),
$$

$$
\frac{P_{L+1}(x)}{P_L(x)}=B_L(x+1)B_L(x+2\alpha+\beta+1)A_L(x+\beta+1)A_L(x+2\alpha+1).
$$

If true, this would imply that the Markov matrix has only $2L$ distinct eigenvalues; the paper supports the formula by explicit calculations, but does not establish it in general.

record.title: The force-based QC spectral equivalence conjecture
record.statement: Let $N\geq4$, let $1\leq K\leq N-2$, and let $F>0$. Denote by $L^{{\rm qcf}}_F$ and $L^{{\rm qnl}}_F$ the force-based and quasinonlocal QC operators, respectively. **Spectral equivalence conjecture.** The operator $L^{{\rm qcf}}_F$ is diagonalizable and has the same spectrum as $L^{{\rm qnl}}_F$. This conjecture concerns the spectral structure underlying iterative methods for the force-based QC approximation; the paper presents numerical evidence but does not establish the assertion analytically.

record.title: The preconditioned force-based QC spectral equivalence conjecture
record.statement: Let $N\geq4$, let $1\leq K\leq N-2$, and let $F>0$. Let ${L}^{-1}$ be the inverse of the discrete Laplacian operator $L$, and consider the preconditioned operators ${L}^{-1}L^{{\rm qcf}}_F$ and ${L}^{-1}L^{{\rm qnl}}_F$. **Preconditioned spectral equivalence conjecture.** The operator ${L}^{-1}L^{{\rm qcf}}_F$ is diagonalizable and has the same spectrum as ${L}^{-1}L^{{\rm qnl}}_F$. This conjecture extends the unpreconditioned spectral observation to the generalized eigenvalue problem used to study preconditioning in the $\mathcal{U}^{1,2}$ setting; the paper supplies numerical evidence but no proof.

record.title: The extremal 2-fold sumgraph conjecture for regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $d,n$ be positive integers, and let $\mathscr{G}$ be a $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, with edge set $\mathscr{E}$. The graph $2\mathscr{G}$ denotes the 2-fold sumgraph, and $K_n$ is the complete graph on $n$ vertices. **The extremal 2-fold sumgraph conjecture.** Either

$$
2\mathscr{G}=K_n,
$$

or

$$
\left|2\mathscr{E}\backslash\mathscr{E}\right|\geq\left(2-o_d(1)\right)n.
$$

The conjecture proposes that, apart from the case where the 2-fold sumgraph is complete, every regular graph has at least approximately $2n$ new edges in its 2-fold sumgraph. The authors are motivated by an explicit family of connected $d$-regular graphs that is essentially extremal for this bound; the conjectural status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Peter Hegarty, “A Cauchy-Davenport type result for arbitrary regular graphs”, arXiv:0910.2250 (2009).

record.title: The projective space derangement graph conjecture for PGL(n+1,q)
record.statement: Let $\mathbb{P}_q^n$ be projective $n$-space, with $n\geq 1$, and let $\Gamma_{\operatorname{PGL}(n+1,q)}$ be the derangement graph of $\operatorname{PGL}(n+1,q)$ acting on $\mathbb{P}_q^n$. An independent set is a set of vertices containing no adjacent pair, and a coset of the stabilizer of a point or hyperplane is a left or right coset of the corresponding setwise stabilizer. **The projective space derangement graph conjecture.** Any independent set of maximal size in $\Gamma_{\operatorname{PGL}(n+1,q)}$ is either the coset of the stabilizer of a point or the coset of the stabilizer of a hyperplane. The source notes that both types attain the maximal size, while for $n\geq 2$ they are not conjugate; no classification beyond these examples is given.

record.title: Conjecture on bias forcing oriented six-cycles
record.statement:
Throughout, let $D$ be an oriented graph, let $n$ be its number of vertices, and let $e(D)$ be its number of arcs. For subsets $A,B\subseteq V(D)$, write $e(A,B)$ for the number of arcs from $A$ to $B$. Define

$$
bias(D):=\max\left\{e(A,B): A,B\subseteq V(D),\ e(B,A)\leq \frac{e(A,B)}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Bias-forcing six-cycle conjecture.** There exists a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every oriented graph $D$ satisfying

$$
bias(D)<\varepsilon\frac{e(D)^{3/2}}{n}
$$

contains an oriented six-cycle.

The paper presents this as a stronger version of its preceding six-cycle theorem, replacing the exponent $2$ by $3/2$. The source gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Strongly minimal covers by independent sets
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph. An **independent set** is a set of vertices containing no edge of $G$, and a cover of the vertex set is a family of such sets whose union is the vertex set. Strong minimality is the dual notion to strong maximality: a cover is strongly minimal when it is no larger, in the corresponding cardinal comparison, than any alternative cover. **Strongly minimal cover conjecture.** Every graph has a strongly minimal cover of its vertex set by independent sets. A positive answer would yield further consequences for posets of bounded width, while the existence of such covers remains open in the stated generality.

record.title: Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n,k$ be natural numbers with $n\geq 4k$, and let $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ be real numbers satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\geq 0.
$$

**Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture.** There exist at least $\binom{n-1}{k-1}$ subsets $A\subseteq [n]$ such that $|A|=k$ and

$$
\sum_{i\in A}x_i\geq 0.
$$

The bound is motivated by assigning one element weight $1$ and each of the remaining $n-1$ elements weight $-1/(n-1)$, for which exactly the $k$-subsets containing the positive element have nonnegative sum. The source presents this as the MMS conjecture in the range $n\geq 4k$; no resolution evidence is supplied here.
